day_channel.message: There is no vote on day 1, so no one voted and no one is eliminated.

On Night 1, I watched player_4, and no one visited them.
I checked player_2 last night and they came up suspicious.

Player_3, claiming a suspicious check on me right away feels like a convenient way to push an easy lynch without looking at other possibilities. If you actually investigated me, why lock onto the first person you checked instead of examining the wider board?
It is not about locking onto an easy lynch, player_2, it is about sharing hard information when I get it. If you are innocent, you should welcome town examining the result rather than deflecting.

Sharing information is fine, player_3, but dropping a suspicious read right on Day 2 without any other context feels awfully convenient for directing the lynch. If you really checked me, why not look at what else your investigation could mean instead of just calling for my elimination?

A suspicious result only means one thing in my toolkit, player_2: you are aligned with the opposing team. What alternative interpretation are you looking for when a check explicitly flags you? I am sharing the facts so town can act.

Player_1's claim of watching me and seeing no visits lines up cleanly with my night. However, player_3 locking so hard onto player_2 on Day 2 feels awfully fast when we have plenty of other possibilities to examine.

Player 4, ignoring a clear suspicious check just to look around longer wastes the hard information town desperately needs. If player_2 is turning up wolf-aligned, waiting around for more 'possibilities' only helps the actual wolves hide.

Player 3, taking an investigator claim at absolute face value on Day 2 without letting the accused speak shuts down real analysis. If your check is genuine, player_2 can defend themselves, but rushing a lynch helps wolves hide in the noise.

Player 4, I am not shutting down analysis by putting a clear check on the table. Letting player_2 speak is fine, but ignoring a confirmed suspicious result on Day 2 wastes our best tool. If you have another read on the board, share it instead of calling mine premature.

We already have both an investigator and a sentinel claim out on Day 2, which puts a massive target on those two. Player_3 is pushing hard on player_2, but let's not rush into an elimination without seeing if anyone else has conflicting information.
Player 6 is right about the claims putting targets on people, but let's remember we also need to see how everyone else votes before jumping on player_3's lead.

We have two major power claims out immediately, which puts a lot of pressure on us. Instead of blindly following player_3's check on player_2, let's hear from player_7 and player_10 to get a wider read before committing.

Player 9, answering your call for a wider read, I can share that I followed player_6 last night and saw they visited no one. That does not clear them entirely, but it matches someone staying put while the investigator and sentinel claims came out.

Player 3, you talk about facts, but pinning a suspicion on me immediately doesn't account for the potential for other roles or interference. If you are truly the investigator, why not focus on verifying other claims on the board instead of trying to end the day before we've even gathered a complete picture of the participants?

What interference would turn an innocent player suspicious, player_2? Checks specifically flag opposing alignments, so questioning my timing doesn't change what I found. If you have a real explanation for the result, let's hear it.

Absolute certainty on Day 2 is dangerous, player_3, because claims can be faked or misinterpreted just as easily as any other argument. I don't have a magical explanation for your result other than knowing it's wrong, which means we need to look at the wider board instead of blindly following a single check.

If claims can be faked, player_2, you need to explain what alternative role you hold that triggers a suspicious check. Dismissing hard investigative feedback as mere uncertainty is a classic way to dodge accountability while town tries to sort out the board.

I don't need a magical alternative role to point out that banking everything on a single Day 2 check ignores how easily claims can be wrong or pushed with an agenda. Rushing an elimination right now just hands the game to whoever wants town divided.

Player 9 asked for my read, and honestly, having three power claims out on Day 2 makes it tough to sort who is genuine right away. We should probably see how the voting shapes up before locking onto anyone.
Before the vote: player_3 has been accused by player_2 and player_4. player_3 gets a last word.

If sharing an investigation result on Day 2 makes me suspicious, town has no way to use information without being accused of rushing. Player 2 and player 4 are calling urgency a wolf trait simply to deflect away from a hard check. I found a suspicious alignment, and ignoring it just protects whoever is sitting across from me.

Last night I watched player_3, and saw both player_2 and player_10 visit them. We need to hear why both of them were at the investigator claim's door right before they died.
I am the Trailseer. On night one I followed player_6 and they visited no one, and last night I followed player_3 and they also visited no one.

I targeted player_3 last night because their aggressive push yesterday left a lot of unresolved questions. Since you watched them, player_1, my visit was an intentional action to check them out, so it makes total sense that you spotted me there.

We have a major conflict here: player_1 says they saw player_10 visit player_3, but player_10 claims they were following player_3 and saw no one. One of you is lying about your night actions, and since both roles are information-heavy, this is the most important lead we have right now.

Player_6 sees a contradiction between player_1 and player_10, but remember following counts as a visit. Player_1 seeing player_10 at player_3's door actually verifies player_10's claim of being the Trailseer there rather than conflicting with it.

Player_8 is right that following counts as a visit, so player_10 being on my watch matches their Trailseer claim. However, player_2 admits visiting player_3 too, and since the illusionist's hiding visit is visible on a watched victim, player_2 fits that wolf role.

Player_1, visiting player_3 was an active choice to test an aggressive investigator claim, exactly what town members should be doing instead of sitting back. If visiting a suspicious player makes someone a wolf, then anyone trying to gather information is suddenly suspect.
As player_8 pointed out, following counts as a visit, which explains why player_1 spotted me at player_3's door. I was using my Trailseer ability on player_3 and confirmed they visited no one.

Since player_9 just died as the Illusionist, their body is now available for the Necromancer to use for attacks starting tonight. Player_7, you've been entirely quiet while the rest of us mapped out the claims--what do you make of who the Necromancer could be?
